headline: Progress Software ordered ShareFile customers to power down their file-sharing servers over a credible active threat, as U.S. courts convicted a Ryuk operator and a Gitea flaw fell under live exploitation.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep turning AI against its own makers, and researchers proved it again with HalluSquatting, which registers the fake package names chatbots invent and turns those hallucinations into remote code execution.
A run of courtroom losses is thinning ransomware's ranks, from a Ryuk operator's guilty plea in Oregon to a BlackCat negotiator's 70-month sentence in Florida.
Enterprise file-sharing and code infrastructure sit in the crosshairs, with Progress pulling the plug on ShareFile servers and a Gitea Docker flaw now under live exploitation.

topics.title: Web and Firmware Flaws Under Active Attack
topics.latest_developments: Attackers began actively exploiting a critical auth-bypass in the official Gitea Docker image that lets them impersonate any user, including administrators, while CISA added actively exploited iCagenda (CVE-2026-48939) and Balbooa Forms (CVE-2026-56291) file-upload flaws to its catalog, Zimbra urged customers to patch a critical Classic Web Client XSS bug, and Binarly disclosed six new U-Boot bootloader flaws.
topics.summary: The bugs span self-hosted Git servers, Joomla extensions, the Zimbra mail suite, and the U-Boot bootloader embedded in routers, cameras, and data-center management chips. Administrators should patch or isolate the affected systems now.

sources.title: Hackers exploit critical auth bypass in Gitea Docker image
CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
Zimbra urges customers to patch critical web client XSS flaw
Six New U-Boot Flaws Could Let Malicious Images Crash Devices or Run Code at Boot

topics.title: Ransomware Operators Face U.S. Prison
topics.latest_developments: A 34-year-old Armenian man pleaded guilty in Oregon federal court to conspiracy and computer fraud for deploying Ryuk ransomware against U.S. companies and faces up to 15 years, the same day a Florida court sentenced former DigitalMint negotiator Angelo Martino, 41, to 70 months for aiding BlackCat/ALPHV extortion.
topics.summary: Ryuk has encrypted hospitals and businesses for large ransoms since 2018; BlackCat/ALPHV ran a ransomware-as-a-service operation dismantled in 2023. U.S. courts are steadily convicting both operators and the insider negotiators who helped them.

sources.title: Ryuk ransomware member pleads guilty in the US, faces 15 years in prison
Ryuk operator pleads guilty; Blackcat/AlphV conspirator gets nearly 6-year sentence
Third US Security Expert Sentenced to Prison for Helping Ransomware Gang

topics.title: Progress ShareFile Emergency Shutdown
topics.latest_developments: Progress Software emailed ShareFile customers on July 10 to immediately shut down the Windows servers running their Storage Zone Controllers, citing a credible external security threat, and temporarily disabled access to affected accounts while it investigates.
topics.summary: ShareFile is Progress Software's enterprise secure file-sharing platform; its on-premises Storage Zone Controllers run on Windows servers. Customers should power the servers off and watch for a fix.

sources.title: URGENT - Progress Tells ShareFile Customers to Shut Down Storage Zone Controllers Over Security Threat
Progress urges ShareFile admins to shut down servers over “credible” threat

topics.title: China and India Both Spy on Balochistan Police
topics.latest_developments: SentinelOne reported that Chinese and Indian state-linked hackers ran separate espionage campaigns against Pakistan's Balochistan Police between February 2024 and April 2026, in some cases breaching the exact same systems.
topics.summary: The Balochistan Police guard Pakistan's southwestern province, site of a long-running separatist insurgency. Rival and allied governments alike targeted the force to harvest intelligence.

sources.title: China, India ran separate spying campaigns against same Pakistani police force
China, India-Linked Hackers Both Targeted Same Pakistani Police Force

topics.title: HalluSquatting Weaponizes AI Hallucinations
topics.latest_developments: Researchers demonstrated HalluSquatting, pre-registering the nonexistent package names that AI coding assistants routinely hallucinate, then serving malware from them to achieve remote code execution and seed a botnet.
topics.summary: When a large language model suggests a library that does not exist, an attacker who has claimed that name delivers malicious code to anyone who follows the suggestion. Verify AI-suggested dependencies before installing them.

sources.title: ‘HalluSquatting’ Turns AI Hallucinations Into Botnet Delivery Mechanism

topics.title: EU Revives Chat Control CSAM Scanning
topics.latest_developments: The European Parliament passed Chat Control 2.0 on July 10, letting companies including Google, Meta, and Microsoft scan users' messages to hunt for child sexual abuse material.
topics.summary: The law revives a contested proposal to permit message scanning across the European Union, reigniting privacy fights over content inspection of private communications.

sources.title: Europe revives law allowing big tech to scan for CSAM

business_politics.title: Senate Deal Tightens Russia Sanctions
business_politics.latest_developments: United States senators reached a deal with the White House on legislation to tighten sanctions on Russia, a potential breakthrough that landed days after Trump signaled a shift toward more support for Kyiv.
business_politics.summary: The bipartisan Senate agreement clears a path to harsher measures against Moscow and its trading partners, and it coincides with Trump's turn toward backing Ukraine—a move that could squeeze Russian energy revenue and the banks and commodities traders exposed to it.

sources.title: US senators strike deal with White House to tighten Russia sanctions

business.title: New Granada Revitalization Enters Phase Two
business.latest_developments: Local and state leaders gathered July 10 to launch Phase Two of the New Granada revitalization in Pittsburgh's Hill District.
business.summary: The project restores the New Granada Theater, a Hill District landmark that Black Masons built nearly a century ago, part of a long push to revive the neighborhood's cultural core.

sources.title: Leaders mark start of next phase of the New Granada revitalization project in Pittsburgh

business.title: Best Places to Work in Western PA Named
business.latest_developments: Organizers released the 2026 Best Places to Work in Western Pennsylvania list July 10.
business.summary: The annual program ranks Pittsburgh-region employers on workplace culture and employee satisfaction, with WPXI publishing the full 2026 honorees.

sources.title: Introducing the 2026 Best Places to Work in Western PA

around_town.title: Wilkinsburg Courts Detoured Drivers
around_town.latest_developments: With the Parkway East closing tonight, the Wilkinsburg Community Development Corporation launched a 'Skip the Tunnel' campaign, plastering billboards to court the up to 100,000 motorists rerouted through the borough for 25 days.
around_town.summary: PennDOT's closure of the Parkway East between the Squirrel Hill Tunnel and the Edgewood/Swissvale exit to replace the Commercial Street Bridge funnels traffic through Wilkinsburg, and the borough's development corporation is pitching those detoured drivers on its vacant office space and businesses with the slogan 'Detour traffic is temporary, tunnel traffic is forever.'

sources.title: Wilkinsburg sees chance to shine during Parkway East closure
Wilkinsburg billboards try to attract new businesses during Parkway East detour: "Tunnel traffic is forever"

around_town.title: Recording Captures CMU President's Trump Dilemma
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource published audio from a year-old Carnegie Mellon staff council meeting in which President Farnam Jahanian called the administration in Washington 'toxic.'
around_town.summary: In the recording, Jahanian described his efforts to shield Carnegie Mellon University, including a decision to paint The Fence, and characterized students as naive, as he weighed a controversial Trump visit to campus.

sources.title: Recording captures CMU president's dilemma, thinking on controversial Trump visit

around_town.title: I-279 and HOV Lanes Close Overnight Next Week
around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT will again close a portion of I-279 and the I-279/I-579 High Occupancy Vehicle lanes overnight next week in Allegheny County.
around_town.summary: The overnight restrictions layer more disruption onto a region already juggling detours from the 25-day Parkway East shutdown that begins tonight.

sources.title: More restrictions, closure planned for I-279, HOV lanes next week

events.title: Wexford Garden and Pond Tour Returns
events.latest_developments: The Wexford Garden and Pond Tour returns Saturday, July 11, after a three-year hiatus.
events.summary: On Saturday, July 11, Wexford homeowners open their yards for the self-guided tour, showing off koi ponds and pondless waterfalls to hundreds of visitors; organizer Debra Krischke promises past favorites and new surprises.

sources.title: Wexford Garden and Pond Tour Returns After Three-Year Hiatus

events.title: Big Boy Steam Locomotive Stops in Leetsdale
events.latest_developments: Union Pacific's Big Boy No. 4014 rolls through western Pennsylvania on Saturday, July 11, ending its return leg with a stop in Leetsdale.
events.summary: The world's largest operating steam locomotive, No. 4014, is crossing the country for America's 250th birthday; after celebrating July 4 in Philadelphia, it passes back through the Pittsburgh area Saturday, July 11, and stops in Leetsdale before heading home west.

sources.title: Here's how to see Big Boy, the world's largest steam locomotive, in western Pennsylvania

around_teams.title: Porter Jr. Eyes a Big Cornerback Payday
around_teams.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette report examined how much the Steelers might pay cornerback Joey Porter Jr. as he seeks an extension in a booming market.
around_teams.summary: Measured against recent deals for corners such as Devon Witherspoon and Christian Gonzalez, Porter, the Steelers' 2023 first-round pick, is positioned to chase a lucrative extension, and the paper weighed how far Pittsburgh will go before training camp opens.

sources.title: Joey Porter Jr. is looking to cash in on a booming market. How much are the Steelers willing to pay?

around_teams.title: Inside the Pirates' Draft of Konnor Griffin
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette detailed how the Pirates landed shortstop Konnor Griffin in the MLB Draft, drawing on general manager Ben Cherington.
around_teams.summary: The account traces how Pittsburgh secured the prized prospect ahead of the White Sox and Nationals; Griffin, now a rookie, has fought through injuries this season, including a jammed finger that could sideline him until September.

sources.title: The inside story of how the Pirates landed Konnor Griffin in the MLB Draft

team_usa.title: USMNT Turns to the 2030 Cycle
team_usa.latest_developments: The Guardian mapped the U.S. men's national team's next three years, flagging sporting director Matt Crocker's abrupt exit for a club job and a pending contract-extension offer to coach Mauricio Pochettino.
team_usa.summary: After the home World Cup ended in a 4-1 round-of-16 loss to Belgium, the United States enters the 2030 cycle facing roster turnover, an unresolved Pochettino decision, and Crocker's departure, with qualifying, the Gold Cup, and Copa América ahead.

sources.title: Time marches on: what the next three years will bring for the USMNT

team_usa.title: Pulisic's World Cup Under Scrutiny
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN weighed whether Christian Pulisic deserves the blame after his home World Cup fell flat.
team_usa.summary: Pulisic, the Milan forward and the U.S. team's biggest star, struggled through the tournament on home soil and left the round-of-16 loss to Belgium with a leg fracture, and ESPN's post-mortem asks how much of the failure lands on him.

sources.title: USMNT's Pulisic flopped at this World Cup, but does he deserve the blame?
